questions.subject: English
questions.stem:
Russians usually live in apartments in tall buildings, and the groom has to climb several stairs to reach his bride. But at each landing he must answer a question to be allowed to go up. The bride’s friends ask difficult questions (sometimes about the bride, sometimes just difficult riddles), and the groom must answer with the help of his friends.

Your group is preparing a short note on marriage customs for the class bulletin board and must explain, from the passage, why a Russian bridegroom cannot reach his bride without help. Choose the option that best explains it. (A) because he is not allowed to enter the building without a written permit from the bride's father (B) because he has to answer a question at every landing and his friends help him to answer (C) because the bride's friends hide the staircase so that he cannot find the right floor (D) because he must pay cash to his friends before they will come with him

answerScheme.modelAnswer: because he has to answer a question at every landing and his friends help him to answer

evidence: But at each landing he must answer a question to be allowed to go up.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem:
A Russian wedding is very simple. The planning only includes arranging for rings, brides’ dress, cars, and a reception. Earlier, the bride’s family paid for the reception, but now-a-days brides’ and grooms’ families usually share expenses. A Russian wedding lasts for two days; some weddings last as long as a week, and the occasion becomes something to remember for years.

A student in your class says that a Russian wedding is very simple to arrange and yet is remembered for years. Choose the option that best explains this on the basis of the passage. (A) because a wedding procession of several cars is the necessary part of the ceremony (B) because the bride's family paid for the reception while the groom's family did not (C) because the wedding lasts two days and the occasion becomes something to remember for years (D) because the bride's friends hide her until the groom has paid a fee

answerScheme.modelAnswer: because the wedding lasts two days and the occasion becomes something to remember for years

evidence: A Russian wedding lasts for two days; some weddings last as long as a week, and the occasion becomes something to remember for years.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your school is holding a Family Values Week, and you have to speak in the morning assembly on the way two families share the work and the cost of a wedding. Write a speech of about 100 words.

markingPoints.description: Content: the speech says that both families now share the expenses of a wedding and that friends also share the work, using the earlier custom as a contrast
Format: the correct format of a speech, that is, a salutation to the audience, the body of the speech and a concluding thank you
Organisation: a clear beginning, a middle part that gives the example of the shared reception and a short conclusion
Accuracy: correct spelling, punctuation, capital letters and a formal tone suitable for a school assembly
Expression: simple sentences and suitable vocabulary that hold the attention of the audience

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Honourable Principal, teachers and dear friends,

A wedding is not the work of one family alone. In earlier days the bride's family paid for the reception all by itself. Now the brides' and grooms' families usually share the expenses. Each side pays its share, and the reception becomes a happy occasion for everybody.

Friends help too. The best friends of the bride and groom meet a few times before the wedding, make posters, write speeches and organise contests. They also answer for the bride when the groom has to prove himself.

So a wedding joins two families and two sets of friends. When the work and the cost are shared, the joy is shared too.

Thank you.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: A classmate asks why the young man says he is already 35 and suffers from palpitations at the very moment he makes his proposal. Explain in about 50 words what he means.

markingPoints.description: He is already 35, which he calls a critical age for marriage
He ought to lead a quiet and regular life and says it is impossible for him not to marry
He suffers from palpitations and is easily upset, so he fears that if he waits for ideal or real love he will never marry

answerScheme.modelAnswer: He means that he cannot afford to wait. He is already 35, which he calls a critical age, and he ought to lead a quiet and regular life. He also suffers from palpitations and is easily upset. So he is afraid that if he hesitates or waits for ideal or real love, he will never marry at all.

In the second place, I ought to lead a quiet and regular life.
If I give myself time to think, to hesitate, to talk a lot, to look for an ideal, or for real love, then I’ll never get married.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: A classmate asks you to trace, in about 120 words and step by step, what happens at a Russian wedding after the newly-married couple leaves the guests for a tour of the city sights. Give your answer in steps.

markingPoints.description: 1: The couple leaves the guests for a tour of the city sights, which lasts two or three hours
2: The couple then arrives at the reception and sits at a specially arranged table with family, friends and invited guests
3: The reception starts with toasts, in which a close friend or relative says a few words and everyone drinks wine at the same moment
4: The groom is then asked to kiss the bride
5: After a few toasts people eat, drink and have fun, and then the bride is stolen and the groom must pay a fee to find her
6: The bride's friends also steal the bride's shoe, the groom must pay for it too, and the guests go on partying

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. The newly-married couple leaves the guests and goes for a tour of the city sights.
2. The tour lasts two or three hours.
3. After the tour the couple arrives at the reception.
4. The couple sits at a specially arranged table with family, friends and invited guests.
5. The reception starts with toasts to the couple: a close friend or relative says a few words to wish them, then everyone raises a glass of wine and drinks at the same moment.
6. The groom is then asked to kiss the bride.
7. After a few toasts people start eating and drinking and generally have fun.
8. After some time the bride is stolen and the groom is asked to pay a fee to find her; usually it is his friends who do it.
9. Then the bride's friends steal the bride's shoe and the groom must pay money for the shoe too, and the guests go on partying.

sits at a specially arranged table with their family, friends and invited guests. The reception starts with toasts to the couple.
Then there are the bride’s friends — they steal the bride’s shoe. The groom must pay money for the shoe too.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: A classmate asks you to trace, in about 120 words and step by step, how the quarrel between the two neighbours over a piece of land called Oxen Meadows grows worse. Give your answer in steps.

markingPoints.description: 1: He claims that his Oxen Meadows touch her birchwoods, and she interrupts to ask whether they are really his
2: He says they are his, she says they are hers, and each repeats that the Meadows belong to her own family
3: He explains that the Meadows are wedged in between her birchwoods and the Burnt Marsh
4: She answers that grandfather and great-grandfather both reckoned their land extended to Burnt Marsh, so the Meadows were theirs
5: He appeals to the documents and says his aunt's grandmother gave the free use of the Meadows in perpetuity to the peasants of her father's grandfather in return for bricks
6: The peasants had the free use for forty years and got into the habit of treating the Meadows as their own, which she refuses to accept, and the quarrel continues

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. The young man tells the young woman that his Oxen Meadows touch her birchwoods.
2. She interrupts him at once and asks whether the Meadows are really his.
3. He says yes; she says they are hers, not his, and he repeats that they are his.
4. He explains that the Meadows are wedged in between her birchwoods and the Burnt Marsh.
5. She answers that grandfather and great-grandfather reckoned their land reached Burnt Marsh, so the Meadows were theirs.
6. He appeals to the documents and says his aunt's grandmother gave the free use of the Meadows in perpetuity to the peasants of her father's grandfather, in return for bricks.
7. Those peasants had the free use for forty years and got into the habit of treating the Meadows as their own.
8. She refuses this story and calls it silly, so the quarrel goes on.

wedged in between your birchwoods and the Burnt Marsh.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: A classmate asks you to explain, in about 120 words and step by step, how the play shows that the marriage was decided by money and land and not by love. Give your answer in steps.

markingPoints.description: 1: The play is about the tendency of wealthy families to seek ties with other wealthy families
2: Their aim is to increase their estates
3: They encourage marriages that make good economic sense
4: Ivan Lomov, a long time wealthy neighbour of the also wealthy Stepan Chubukov, comes to ask for the hand of his twenty-five-year-old daughter Natalya
5: He is large and hearty but very suspicious, and he quarrels over petty issues, so the proposal is in danger of being forgotten
6: Even so, economic good sense ensures that the proposal is made, after all, although the quarrelling perhaps continues

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. The play is about the tendency of wealthy families to seek ties with other wealthy families.
2. Their aim is to increase their estates.
3. They do this by encouraging marriages that make good economic sense.
4. So Ivan Lomov, a long time wealthy neighbour of Stepan Chubukov, who is also wealthy, comes to seek the hand of Chubukov's twenty-five-year-old daughter, Natalya.
5. He is a large and hearty, but very suspicious, landowner, and he quarrels with her at once over the Meadows he says are his.
6. All three are quarrelsome people, and they quarrel over petty issues.
7. Because of this quarrelling the proposal is in danger of being forgotten.
8. Yet economic good sense ensures that the proposal is made, after all.
9. The quarrelling perhaps continues, but the match goes through.
